headline: Brazil Selic Rate Cut Proposal Sparks Foreign Reserves and Real Warning
summary: A Brazilian economist warned that halving the 13.75% Selic benchmark interest rate could trigger a run on the real and strain the nation's $367.9 billion in foreign reserves.
why: Brazil's Selic rate is a primary anchor for domestic inflation and capital flows; sudden cuts can prompt currency depreciation and capital outflows.

impacts.name: Brazilian Real
impacts.why: Economists caution that an aggressive reduction from the 13.75% benchmark could trigger currency depreciation and reserve pressure.
